summary: Added Modbus RTU (serial) and RTU-over-TCP transports, so a Modbus device no longer has to be reachable over Modbus TCP/MBAP. infra/iot/modbus gained a transport abstraction: a shared `transport` interface splits the original MBAP-over-TCP framing (`mbapTransport`, moved out of client.go with no behavior change; `Dial` is unchanged) from a new RTU framing (`rtuTransport`, transport.go) used by both a serial line and a raw TCP socket -- RTU has no length header, so the response size is inferred from the request's function code, and every frame is checked against a Modbus RTU CRC-16 (new crc.go: crc16/appendCRC/crcOK). A new `DialRTUTCP` opens RTU framing over a plain TCP socket, for transparent RS485-to-TCP gateways that don't speak real Modbus TCP. A new serial.go adds `SerialParams` (baud/parity/data-bits/stop-bits, defaulting to the near-universal 9600 8N1), `DialSerial`, and a per-port mutex registry so several unit ids sharing one physical RS485 bus are polled one at a time rather than colliding -- backed by a new pure-Go dependency, go.bug.st/serial v1.8.0 (no cgo, keeping the single-binary/air-gapped posture). `DeviceConf` gained `Transport` (TCP/RTU-over-TCP/Serial) and `Serial SerialParams`, and a `dial()` helper both `PollOnce` and `WriteConfirm` now use, so SunSpec auto-discovery, register-map reads, and guarded control writes all work unchanged over any of the three transports. On the app side, `entities.IotDevice` gained `Transport`/`Baud`/`Parity`/`DataBits`/`StopBits` (for serial, Endpoint holds the port name -- COM3, /dev/ttyUSB0 -- instead of host:port), plumbed through device create/update requests and a new `modbusTransportOf` helper the poller's `planFor` uses to build each device's `DeviceConf`. The guarded-write seam in CommandService (`modbusWriteFunc`) changed shape from a bare (endpoint, unit, reg, value, timeout) to (modbus.DeviceConf, reg, value, timeout) so a control write inherits the device's transport exactly like a poll does, and now wires directly to modbus.WriteConfirm with no wrapper needed. The frontend device editor gained a shared ModbusFields component: a Transport select (Modbus TCP / RTU over TCP / Serial) plus, for serial, port name and baud/parity/data-bits/stop-bits fields, with new en i18n keys.
compatibility: Fully additive and backward-compatible for every existing install. Transport defaults to the zero value (TCP/MBAP) both on the wire (modbus.Transport's TransportTCP=0) and on the device row (empty string maps to TCP via modbusTransportOf), so every device configured before this change keeps dialing Modbus TCP exactly as it did, with no migration needed. The new go.bug.st/serial dependency is only exercised when a device's transport is explicitly set to serial; it adds no new listening surface. Adopting a serial or RTU-over-TCP device requires the physical host running myiotsan to actually have that serial port or TCP gateway reachable -- getting the transport/line settings wrong fails the poll (and any control write) cleanly rather than silently misreading, the same fail-closed posture the existing Modbus TCP path already has.
